title: Concrete Structures: Numerical Practice Set 1 (Moderate to Hard)
instructions: All 40 questions are numerical, of moderate to hard level, based on IS 456:2000. Keep rough paper ready.
Use the code values and factors given in each question.

questions.question: A singly reinforced beam with Fe 415 steel has an effective depth of 500 mm. Taking x_u,max/d = 0.48 as per IS 456:2000, the limiting depth of the neutral axis is:
questions.explanation: x_u,max = 0.48d = 0.48 × 500 = 240 mm. (The ratio is 0.53 for Fe 250 and 0.46 for Fe 500.)

questions.question: A rectangular beam is 250 mm wide with an effective depth of 500 mm, in M20 concrete and Fe 415 steel. Using M_u,lim = 0.138 f_ck b d², its limiting moment of resistance is:

questions.explanation: x_u = 200.58 mm, less than x_u,max = 0.48 × 450 = 216 mm, so the section is under-reinforced. M_u = 0.87 f_y A_st (d − 0.42x_u) = 361050 × (450 − 84.24) ≈ 132.06 kN·m.

A beam 300 mm wide with an effective depth of 500 mm has 2500 mm² of Fe 500 tension steel in M25 concrete (x_u,max/d = 0.46). The moment of resistance to be used in design, as per IS 456, is approximately:
questions.explanation: x_u = 0.87 × 500 × 2500 / (0.36 × 25 × 300) = 402.8 mm, more than x_u,max = 230 mm, so the section is over-reinforced and is limited to M_u,lim = 0.36 f_ck b x_u,max (d − 0.42x_u,max) = 0.36 × 25 × 300 × 230 × (500 − 96.6) ≈ 250.51 kN·m.

questions.question: A doubly reinforced beam must resist a factored moment of 250 kN·m. The limiting moment of the singly reinforced section is 172.5 kN·m. With d = 500 mm, d′ = 50 mm and Fe 415 steel, the additional tension steel A_st2 required is approximately:

A T-beam floor (monolithic slab and beams) has beams at 3 m centres with a web width of 300 mm and a flange thickness of 120 mm. The distance between points of zero moment is 6 m. As per IS 456, the effective flange width is:
questions.explanation: b_f = l₀/6 + b_w + 6D_f = 6000/6 + 300 + 6 × 120 = 2020 mm, which is less than the beam spacing of 3000 mm, so b_f = 2020 mm.

questions.explanation: Shear carried by concrete = τ_c b d = 0.5 × 300 × 500 = 75 kN. V_us = 180 − 75 = 105 kN.

questions.explanation: A_st,min = 0.12% × 1000 × 150 = 180 mm² per metre. (For mild steel it is 0.15%, giving 225 mm².)

questions.question: A slab needs 350 mm² of main steel per metre width. Using 10 mm diameter bars, the required centre-to-centre spacing is approximately:
questions.explanation: Area of one 10 mm bar = 78.54 mm². Spacing = 1000 × 78.54 / 350 ≈ 224.4 mm.

questions.question: A two-way slab has a short span of 4 m and carries a factored load of 12 kN/m². If the short-span moment coefficient α_x is 0.062, the design moment per metre width in the short direction is approximately:
questions.explanation: M_x = α_x w l_x² = 0.062 × 12 × 4² ≈ 11.90 kN·m per metre.

questions.question: A short, axially loaded column is 400 mm × 400 mm with 2000 mm² of Fe 415 longitudinal steel in M25 concrete. As per IS 456, its factored axial load capacity is approximately:
A short circular column of 400 mm diameter has helical reinforcement and 1600 mm² of Fe 415 longitudinal steel in M20 concrete. As per IS 456, its factored axial load capacity is approximately:
questions.explanation: A_c = (π/4) × 400² − 1600 = 124064 mm². Capacity with ties = 0.4 × 20 × 124064 + 0.67 × 415 × 1600 = 1437.4 kN. A helically reinforced column takes 1.05 times this: ≈ 1509.3 kN.

questions.question: A column has an unsupported length of 3 m and a lateral dimension of 450 mm. As per IS 456, the minimum eccentricity to be considered in this direction is:
questions.explanation: e_min = L/500 + D/30 = 3000/500 + 450/30 = 6 + 15 = 21 mm, which is more than the 20 mm minimum, so e_min = 21 mm.

questions.question: A column is 300 mm × 450 mm with an unsupported length of 4 m. The effective length factor is 0.8 in both directions. The slenderness ratio about the minor axis is approximately:
questions.explanation: Effective length = 0.8 × 4000 = 3200 mm. Slenderness ratio = l_e / b = 3200 / 300 ≈ 10.67 (less than 12, so it is a short column).

questions.question: A column 300 mm × 500 mm has 16 mm diameter longitudinal bars. As per IS 456, the maximum pitch of the lateral ties is:
questions.explanation: Pitch is the least of: the least lateral dimension (300 mm), 16 × the smallest longitudinal bar diameter (16 × 16 = 256 mm), and 300 mm. So the pitch is 256 mm.

questions.question: A column carries a service load of 1000 kN. The self-weight of the footing is taken as 10% of the column load and the safe bearing capacity of the soil is 200 kN/m². The side of a square footing should be approximately:
A square footing 2.5 m × 2.5 m supports a 400 mm × 400 mm column. The factored net upward soil pressure is 240 kN/m². The design bending moment at the face of the column is:
questions.explanation: Cantilever projection = (2.5 − 0.4) / 2 = 1.05 m. M_u = q B × (projection)² / 2 = 240 × 2.5 × 1.05² / 2 = 330.75 kN·m.

A rectangular prestressed beam 300 mm × 600 mm carries a prestressing force of 900 kN at an eccentricity of 100 mm below the centroid. Ignoring self-weight, the stress at the bottom fibre is:
questions.explanation: P/A = 900000 / 180000 = 5 MPa. Pe/Z = 900000 × 100 / (300 × 600² / 6) = 5 MPa. Bottom fibre stress = 5 + 5 = 10 MPa (compression); the top fibre stress is zero.
